title: 3.3 Cell Types
description: Prokaryotic vs eukaryotic cells and plant vs animal cells

questions.question: What is the main difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Prokaryotic cells are larger than eukaryotic cells
Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus, while eukaryotic cells have a true nucleus
Prokaryotic cells have mitochondria, eukaryotic cells do not
questions.explanation: The key difference is that prokaryotic cells have no membrane-bound nucleus (their DNA is in a nucleoid region), while eukaryotic cells have a true nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a prokaryotic organism?
questions.explanation: E. coli is a bacterium and therefore a prokaryote. Amoeba, yeast, and human cells are eukaryotes.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a eukaryotic organism?
questions.explanation: Human liver cells are eukaryotic (having a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles). Bacteria and archaea are prokaryotes.

questions.question: Which structure is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose outside the cell membrane, which animal cells lack.

questions.question: Which structure is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts (for photosynthesis) are found in plant cells but not in animal cells.

questions.question: Which structure is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cells contain a large central vacuole that stores water and maintains turgor pressure; animal cells have smaller vacuoles if any.

questions.question: What shape do most plant cells have?
questions.explanation: Plant cells are typically rectangular or have a fixed, regular shape due to the rigid cell wall, while animal cells are more irregular or round.

questions.question: What shape do most animal cells have?
questions.explanation: Animal cells typically have irregular, round, or variable shapes because they lack a rigid cell wall.

questions.question: Do prokaryotic cells have ribosomes?
options: Yes, but they are smaller (70S) than eukaryotic ribosomes (80S)
Yes, they are identical to eukaryotic ribosomes
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells have 70S ribosomes (smaller), while eukaryotic cells have 80S ribosomes (larger).

questions.question: Where is the DNA located in a prokaryotic cell?
options: In the nucleoid region (a region of the cytoplasm without a membrane)
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic DNA is found in the nucleoid region — a concentrated area in the cytoplasm that is not enclosed by a membrane.

questions.question: Which of the following organelles is found in eukaryotic cells but NOT in prokaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are membrane-bound organelles found only in eukaryotic cells. Prokaryotes lack all membrane-bound organelles.

questions.question: Do prokaryotic cells have a cell wall?
options: No, they only have a cell membrane
Yes, most have a cell wall (peptidoglycan in bacteria)
Only some prokaryotes have a cell wall
They have a cell wall made of cellulose
questions.explanation: Most prokaryotic cells (bacteria) have a cell wall made of peptidoglycan, which provides structural support.

questions.question: What is the typical size range of prokaryotic cells compared to eukaryotic cells?
options: Prokaryotes are smaller (0.1-5 $\mu$m), eukaryotes are larger (10-100 $\mu$m)
They are approximately the same size
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells are generally much smaller (0.1-5 $\mu$m), while eukaryotic cells are larger (10-100 $\mu$m).

questions.question: Which of the following is found in animal cells but NOT in plant cells?
questions.explanation: Centrioles (involved in cell division) are found in animal cells but not in most plant cells.

questions.question: What is the storage form of carbohydrates in plant cells?
questions.explanation: Plants store carbohydrates as starch, while animal cells store carbohydrates as glycogen.

questions.question: What is the storage form of carbohydrates in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Animal cells store excess glucose as glycogen (mainly in liver and muscle cells), while plants store it as starch.

questions.question: Which type of cell division occurs in prokaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells reproduce by binary fission — a simple division process where the DNA replicates and the cell divides into two identical cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the genetic material of prokaryotic cells?
options: It is linear and contained within a nucleus
It is typically a single circular chromosome located in the nucleoid region
It is found in multiple linear chromosomes inside a nucleus
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic DNA consists of a single circular chromosome located in the nucleoid region, unlike the linear chromosomes in eukaryotic nuclei.

questions.question: What is the main reason plant cells are able to maintain a fixed rectangular shape?
options: They have a large central vacuole
They have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose
questions.explanation: The rigid cell wall of cellulose provides structural support and maintains the fixed rectangular shape of plant cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a prokaryotic organism?
options: Lactobacillus (a bacterium used in yogurt production)
questions.explanation: Lactobacillus is a bacterium and therefore prokaryotic. Paramecium, mushrooms (fungi), and Euglena are eukaryotes.

questions.question: Which group of organisms is classified as having eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Eukaryotes include all members of the kingdoms Animalia, Plantae, Fungi, and Protista — organisms with true nuclei and membrane-bound organelles.

questions.question: What is the main difference in the cell wall composition between bacteria and plant cells?
options: Bacterial cell walls are made of cellulose; plant cell walls are made of peptidoglycan
Bacterial cell walls contain peptidoglycan; plant cell walls contain cellulose
Both have cell walls made of the same material
Bacteria do not have cell walls
questions.explanation: Bacterial cell walls are made of peptidoglycan (a polymer of sugars and amino acids), while plant cell walls are made of cellulose.

questions.question: Do plant cells contain lysosomes?
options: Yes, plant cells contain many lysosomes for digestion
No, plant cells do not have lysosomes; the vacuole performs some digestive functions
questions.explanation: Most plant cells lack lysosomes. The central vacuole in plant cells can perform some digestive and waste-removal functions.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the large central vacuole in plant cells?
options: Water storage and maintenance of turgor pressure
questions.explanation: The large central vacuole stores water, maintains turgor pressure that keeps the plant rigid, and also stores nutrients and waste products.

questions.question: Which kingdom consists entirely of prokaryotic organisms?
questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera (Eubacteria and Archaebacteria) consists entirely of prokaryotic organisms.

questions.question: What is the size of eukaryotic ribosomes?
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S (larger), while prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S (smaller).

questions.question: What is the size of prokaryotic ribosomes?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S, composed of a 50S large subunit and a 30S small subunit.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a difference between plant and animal cells?
questions.explanation: Both plant and animal cells contain mitochondria. The differences include cell wall, chloroplasts, vacuoles, and shape.

questions.question: What is the function of plasmids in prokaryotic cells?
options: They are small circular DNA molecules that carry extra genes (e.g., antibiotic resistance)
questions.explanation: Plasmids are small, circular DNA molecules separate from the main chromosome, often carrying genes for antibiotic resistance or other advantages.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?
options: Prokaryotes can be unicellular, and all eukaryotes are multicellular
Prokaryotes are always unicellular; eukaryotes can be unicellular or multicellular
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes are always unicellular. Eukaryotes can be unicellular (e.g., amoeba, yeast) or multicellular (e.g., humans, trees).
